goal: Explain how a cross-device Agent workspace uses one local Git authority, read-only projections, and same-SHA handoff without treating a cloud service as the primary memory source.
narrative: Agents load a bootstrap contract, retrieve context from read-only projections, act through tools, submit validated candidates to local Git main, and project the accepted SHA to backups, indexes, and Skills.
scope: Logical responsibilities from Agent entry through local authority, projections, integrations, backup, and raw artifact stores; deployment topology and concrete auth protocols are outside scope.
must_show: Multiple device and Agent entry points
Local Git main as the only writable long-term authority
GitHub as same-SHA backup and handoff
Request to retrieval to candidate acceptance to projection loop
emphasize: Local Git main is authoritative while clients read projections
GitHub backup and raw file storage have distinct responsibilities
Only validated candidates enter the long-term source
relationships: Clients load bootstrap and capability routes
Validated candidates update local Git main
The accepted SHA is backed up to GitHub and projected locally
Raw assets persist to file stores
uncertainties: The exact authentication protocol is unspecified
The exact backup transport and local index implementation are unspecified
assumptions: Permission boundaries are shown as a routing responsibility without naming a protocol
The architecture is logical rather than a deployment topology
content_risks: Do not imply read-only projections can accept writes
Do not imply GitHub is the local writable authority
Do not imply the long-term source stores every raw file
Do not invent trust zones or runtime regions
Do not give every integration the same weight as the authority/projection distinction
quality_questions: Can a viewer identify local Git main as the only writable long-term authority within five seconds?
Are read-only projections visibly distinct from backup and raw-file storage?
Is the request to context to execution to candidate acceptance to projection path obvious?
Are logical responsibilities separated from unspecified implementation details?
Are external tools visibly integrations rather than authoritative memory stores?
